title: Understanding pedagogical challenges faced by technology teachers in special needs classrooms
abstract: <jats:p>Teaching learners with special educational needs requires dynamic and adaptive pedagogical strategies that can lead to social development and academic success. This can be possible if teachers are assisted in mitigating the daily challenges of teaching such learners. This qualitative exploratory case study investigated the pedagogical challenges encountered by two Grade 9 Technology teachers in the Capricorn District of Limpopo Province. This study used Shulman’s Content and Pedagogical Knowledge framework to understand teachers’ challenges. Data was collected through semi-structured interviews and classroom observations; all collected data were analysed thematically. This study found that teachers experienced various challenges, including the emotional labour of teaching, burnout in the LSEN environment and the enactment of instructional knowledge. The study concluded that the sampled teachers displayed weaknesses in lesson planning, activating learners’ prior knowledge, diagnosing errors, achieving curriculum objectives and sustaining engagement. As a result, it was recommended that support through teacher assistants, creative differentiated strategies and enhanced digital-technology literacy to improve outcomes for learners with special needs was imminent.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Education and Learning Technology

title: Integration of Biomechanics and Digital Technology: Using Kinovea for Motion Analysis and Learning for Beginner Athletes
abstract:
<jats:p>Background: The integration of biomechanics with digital motion-analysis technologies has introduced new approaches for examining movement efficiency, kinematic characteristics, and technical patterns in walking and running activities. Kinovea, as an accessible motion-analysis software, provides both visual and quantitative feedback. However, its application in supporting technique development among beginner athletes remains insufficiently explored.
Aim: This study aims to describe the use of Kinovea in biomechanics training and examine its contribution to the awareness of kinematic characteristics and movement techniques among beginner athletes.
Methods: A descriptive qualitative design involved 72 beginner athletes aged 18–25 years selected through purposive sampling. Data were collected over 16 weeks through interviews, field observations, and motion video recordings analyzed using Kinovea. Kinematic data focused on joint angles, stride behavior, and movement phases during walking, running, and the flight phase. Qualitative data were analyzed using content analysis with NVivo 12, while kinematic results were interpreted descriptively to identify performance patterns and areas for technical refinement.
Result: Kinematic analysis showed coordinated joint-angle patterns across all phases. Walking analysis identified arm swing angles of 50.9°–58.8° and leg separation angles of 64.3°–67.2°, indicating a stable gait rhythm. The running analysis revealed knee angles of 68.8°–69.8° and elbow angles of 87.6°–89.1°, indicating efficient propulsive mechanics. The flight phase demonstrated knee angles of 81.2°–87.8° and elbow angles of 80.4°–88.3°, suggesting effective momentum use and postural stability. These measurements supported stride-efficiency assessment and technique evaluation. Qualitative findings revealed that Kinovea enabled athletes to interpret movement phases and identify technical inefficiencies through slow-motion and frame-by-frame visualization.
Conclusion: Kinovea supports basic motion analysis by providing clear kinematic information and helping beginner athletes observe and refine their movement techniques. The findings also offer practical value for coaches by enabling more precise identification of inefficient patterns and guiding targeted corrections during early-stage training.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Coaching and Sports Science

title: HYBRID NETWORK INTRUSION DETECTION SYSTEM BASED ON SIGNATURE ANALYSIS AND MACHINE LEARNING METHODS
abstract: <jats:p>In the context of increasing complexity of modern network infrastructures and the growing number of cyberattacks, improving the effectiveness of intrusion detection systems is a highly relevant task. The aim of this work is to develop and investigate a hybrid approach to network attack detection based on a combination of signature-based analysis and intelligent machine learning methods.  The research methods include analysis of requirements for anomaly detection systems, comparative analysis of existing solutions, design of a hybrid system architecture, and experimental modeling using multiclass classification of network traffic. The results demonstrate that integrating a neural model with a traditional detection system improves attack detection coverage and reduces the number of false positives.  The practical significance of the study lies in the possibility of deploying the proposed architecture in real corporate networks, while the theoretical significance consists in substantiating the effectiveness of a hybrid approach to traffic analysis. Future research directions include adaptive model training and expansion of the range of detectable attacks.</jats:p>

title: A Review of Phishing Detection Techniques Using Machine Learning and Natural Language Processing
abstract: <jats:p>The goal of phishing attacks, which rank high among cyber risks, is to steal sensitive information (such as login passwords, financial data, and more) from unsuspecting people and companies. Blacklist, whitelist, rule, heuristic, and signature-based detection methods are no longer suitable due to the rising sophistication of phishing schemes. As a result, ML, DL, and NLP are rapidly becoming into effective instruments for detecting both well-known and brand-new forms of phishing. Background on phishing assaults, old ways of detecting them, and recent advances in intelligent phishing detection are all included in this article. It delves into several machine learning algorithms such as decision tree, LSTM, ANN, CNN, and RNN, as well as deep learning models like KNN, NB, and SVM. Also, natural language processing methods including word embedding, sentiment analysis, text categorization, and tokenization are explored with the aim of detecting phishing material. Presenting a comprehensive, precise, and up-to-the-minute phishing detection system is the ultimate goal of this study, which focuses on machine learning frameworks, performance indicators, present obstacles, and future research directions.</jats:p>
venue: Journal of Global Research in Multidisciplinary Studies(JGRMS)

title: Cyber Defense Digital Twins: A Federated Learning and Zero-Trust AI Architecture for Autonomous Threat Prediction and Response
abstract: <jats:p>Modern enterprise networks operate under persistent threats that exploit cloud-native misconfigurations, identity sprawl, and API vulnerabilities at machine speed. Existing security operations center (SOC) architectures remain largely reactive, signature-dependent, and incapable of predicting multi-stage lateral movement. This paper proposes the Cognitive Cyber Defense Digital Twin (CCDT), a unified architecture integrating federated learning (FL), graph neural network (GNN)-based attack-path forecasting, adversarially hardened detection models, and autonomous Security Orchestration, Automation, and Response (SOAR) with deception engineering. The CCDT constructs a continuously synchronized digital replica of organizational assets and employs reinforcement learning-based red agents to stress-test detection models. A federated intelligence mesh enables cross-organizational privacy-preserving gradient sharing. Experimental evaluations against CICIDS-2018 and LANL datasets demonstrate 52% faster attack-path detection, 41% reduction in false positive rate, and 60% reduction in mean-time-to-respond (MTTR) compared to traditional SOC baselines. Integrated Explainable AI (XAI) modules using SHAP values enable audit-ready compliance reporting. The CCDT represents a paradigm shift from reactive monitoring to predictive, autonomous, and privacy-preserving cyber defense for hybrid cloud environments.</jats:p>
venue: International Journal of Scientific Research in Computer Science, Engineering and Information Technology

title: Association of Human Immunodeficiency Virus Infection With Reduced Helicobacter pylori Positivity: Findings From Four Diagnostic Tests.
abstract: Sub-Saharan Africa has the highest burden of both Human Immunodeficiency virus (HIV) and Helicobacter pylori (H. pylori) infections. The acquisition and disease manifestation of these two infections are different, but both are chronic and cannot be spontaneously cleared by human immunological mechanisms. We sought to determine the association between HIV and H. pylori infection in a cohort from Zambia. We prospectively enrolled patients presenting for upper gastrointestinal endoscopy and tested them for HIV and H. pylori infection. HIV testing was performed serologically using Determine for screening and Tri-Dot for confirmation. The presence of H. pylori infection was determined by serology, histology, stool antigen, and rapid urease testing. Patient demographic details were collected using interviewer-administered questionnaires. Data were analysed using R statistical software employing standard methods. Among the 300 participants enrolled, 61 (20%) were HIV-positive and 239 (80%) were HIV-negative. Overall, H. pylori positivity was significantly lower in HIV-positive than in HIV-negative participants (65% vs. 81%; p = 0.015). HIV-positive participants had lower positivity rates by serology (51% vs. 72%; OR: 0.40, 95% CI: 0.21-0.76), histology (20% vs. 36%; OR: 0.45, 95% CI: 0.22-0.87), and rapid urease test (15% vs. 30%; OR: 0.42, 95% CI: 0.18-0.86). Stool antigen positivity did not differ significantly by HIV status. Using a composite reference standard for active infection, plasma serology showed lower sensitivity (63.2% vs. 83.7%) and accuracy (61.9% vs. 81.3%) in HIV-positive participants than in HIV-negative participants. Among participants with active H. pylori infection, HIV-positive individuals were nearly three times more likely to have false-negative serology results (OR: 2.97; p = 0.06). HIV-positive individuals demonstrate lower H. pylori positivity and reduced serological test performance than HIV-negative individuals. Therefore, serology may underestimate active H. pylori infections in people living with HIV.

title: Prototype-based geometry of local object patches in the pigeon mesopallium ventrolaterale.
abstract: In natural vision, objects are frequently partially occluded and thus perceived through local fragments, yet how such fragments are organized in neural representational space remains poorly understood. Using pigeons (  在自然视觉场景中，物体常常会被遮挡，动物只能通过局部碎片信息完成物体识别。然而，这些局部碎片在神经表征空间中是如何组织的，仍缺乏清晰认识。该研究以鸽子为模型，结合整体–局部图像分类行为范式与被动观看条件下MVL群体电生理记录，系统探讨了局部图像碎片的神经表征结构。我们采用CEBRA-time方法将神经时间序列嵌入到低维表征空间，并以整体图像诱发的群体神经响应定义类别神经原型，再将局部图像块投射到同一空间中，通过其与原型之间的距离，定量分析原型距离与行为识别准确率及图像语义成分之间的关系。研究结果表明，在MVL中，动物类别的局部图像块呈现出紧凑的、以原型为中心的聚类结构。跨图像块分析发现，原型距离越大，鸽子的行为识别准确率越低；而更接近原型的图像块，则更富集于头部、面部等具有诊断意义的关键语义部位。相比之下，在多个深度神经网络基线模型中，原型距离既无法稳定预测行为表现，也不能一致反映图像块的语义分布特征。在此基础上，研究进一步提出了一种局部原型学习机制，使类别匹配由局部特征与学习得到的原型之间的接近程度所决定。引入该机制后，网络能够重现多项与MVL一致的几何表征特征，包括动物类别的原型中心化聚类结构，以及原型距离与行为表现之间的负相关关系。该研究支持了这样一种观点：鸽子MVL对不完整目标的表征，遵循一种与关键诊断部位相关的原型式几何组织原则；同时，这一发现也为构建类脑视觉模型提供了可操作的神经约束。.

title: AI-powered virtual cells, digital twins and agentic AI are reshaping multi-omics, spatial biology and drug discovery.
abstract: Predicting individual disease trajectories and treatment responses remains challenging in drug discovery. Molecular profiling provides static snapshots that miss cellular dynamics, spatial context and adaptive responses. The convergence of single-cell and spatial omics with generative AI is driving a paradigm shift toward AI-powered virtual cells that model cellular states, interactions and treatment responses. This review introduces a nested framework of six capabilities for AI-powered virtual cells, spanning population-derived models, digital twins and agentic twins. Virtual cells generate synthetic cellular states and predict responses from population data. Digital twins link models to specific biological counterparts, enabling longitudinal updating and prospective prediction. Agentic twins add spatial context, biologically constrained interactions and actions, and environmental feedback, enabling personalized, dynamic and interactive representations of cellular ecosystems. This narrative review is based on literature acquired from PubMed, Web of Science, bioRxiv and arXiv searches up to October 2026. AI-powered virtual cells could support drug discovery as foundation models that transfer biological knowledge across tasks, including data-limited settings. Their value depends on faithful extrapolation beyond training data and prospective validation against biological observations. Coupling these models to repeatedly measured experimental systems could enable personalized prediction, iterative updating and prioritization of perturbations, targets and therapeutic strategies.

title: ANCHOR: AI-NGS consensus hierarchy for optimized refinement of high-affinity binders from affinity maturation.
abstract: Affinity maturation for the systematic discovery of high-affinity protein reagents remains a major challenge in display-based protein engineering, largely because phenotypic enrichment frequently fails to correlate with true binding affinity. To improve candidate identification, we developed ANCHOR, an artificial intelligence (AI) and next-generation sequencing (NGS) consensus hierarchy for optimized refinement that implements a score-decoupled, two-stage strategy. Enrichment-trained classifier and regression models are used to construct a candidate pool, from which group-specific consensus sequences are subsequently derived without ranking candidates solely by individual model scores. Using the phosphotyrosine-binding Fyn SH2 domain as a model system, the two models achieved strong performance on untouched independent test sets (classification area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUROC) = 0.974; regression Pearson's r = 0.870). By leveraging a biopanning-guided filter, ANCHOR reduced the searchable sequence space by approximately four orders of magnitude while maintaining a ~90% overlap with exhaustive screening and retained 297 enrichment-predicted variants. These variants were grouped by residue identity at the least-conserved position (P4) and consensus sequences were derived within each group. Among the 16 evaluable consensus variants, 9 (56%) matched or exceeded the affinity of TrM, a previously established 100-fold-improved superbinder, with several showing a two-fold further improvement. Exploratory analyses using a structural proxy indicated robustness to parameter choices and a higher observed hit rate for ANCHOR than for the evaluated alternatives. Application to a public anti-HER2 scFv yeast-display NGS dataset demonstrated computational portability across datasets and library designs. Collectively, ANCHOR provides a practical framework for prioritizing affinity-maturation candidates from display-derived NGS data.

title: Integrating Unsupervised and Supervised Learning for Robust Identification of Hip Osteoarthritis Morphological Features.
abstract: This case-control observational study aimed to determine whether an integrated multivariate analytical framework combining complementary unsupervised and supervised learning methods can identify reproducible radiographic and clinical features associated with hip osteoarthritis (OA) status. A total of 216 participants (155 OA patients and 61 controls) underwent clinical assessment and standardized radiographic evaluation, with morphological measurements obtained from anteroposterior, Dunn and frog-leg lateral (LL) views. A two-stage analytical approach combined Principal Component Analysis and Hierarchical Cluster Analysis with Orthogonal Partial Least Squares Discriminant Analysis and Random Forest. Model robustness was assessed using cross-validation, permutation testing and class-balancing strategies. Unsupervised analyses revealed modest but significant morphological differences between OA patients and controls, with substantial overlap reflecting disease heterogeneity. Supervised models demonstrated moderate predictive performance. Clinical variables, particularly functional status and pain measures, were the strongest discriminators between groups. Among morphological features, the alpha angle consistently showed the highest variable importance across all projections and analytical approaches, alongside the Singh index, head-neck offset ratio and pistol grip deformity. Inclusion of LL measurements did not improve model performance and in some cases reduced discriminatory power. Hip OA was associated with subtle but consistent morphological differences rather than distinct structural separation from controls. Across complementary multivariate analyses, proximal femoral morphology, particularly the alpha angle, showed the most consistent association with OA status. These findings suggest that integrated multivariate analytical approaches can help identify reproducible OA-associated radiographic features and provide a framework for future studies investigating morphological phenotypes of hip OA.

title: Spatiotemporal water quality assessment of Xingqing Lake, China: Integrating water quality index, principal component analysis, and machine learning for SDG 6 reporting.
abstract: Urban lakes are increasingly affected by stormwater runoff, wastewater inputs, and intensive human activities, while water-quality assessments increasingly combine indices, multivariate statistics, and machine learning (ML) but often emphasize different stages of assessment, diagnosis, prediction, or management. This study introduces an integrated water quality index (WQI)-principal component analysis (PCA)-ML framework for comprehensive water-quality assessment, demonstrated through a case study at Xingqing Lake, China (2022-2025). The study analyzed seven parameters (pH, dissolved oxygen, permanganate chemical oxygen demand, dichromate chemical oxygen demand, 5-day biochemical oxygen demand [BOD Lake water quality faces pollution from streets, sewage, and parks. From 2022 to 2025, we tested water monthly at five sites in Xingqing Lake, China. We measured seven indicators (pH, dissolved oxygen, permanganate chemical oxygen demand, dichromate chemical oxygen demand, biochemical oxygen demand, NH4+‐N, and total phosphorus). Three methods were combined: a water quality index to score overall health, principal component analysis to find pollution sources, and machine learning (ML) to predict future quality. Results showed clear spatial patterns: one site was “excellent,” two were “good,” two were “poor” or “medium.” Ammonia, organic waste, and phosphorus were the main pollutants. ML predicted water quality with 92% accuracy. The framework helps cities report progress on UN Sustainable Development Goal 6 (Clean Water).

title: [Modern possibilities for the diagnosis of voice disorders using computer acoustic analysis of voice and artificial intelligence].
abstract: To evaluate the effectiveness of different AI models in diagnosing dysphonia based on acoustic voice analysis, and to compare the accuracy and predictive value of algorithms in distinguishing normal condition, functional and organic voice disorders. The study included 1260 patients divided into three groups: those with normal voice function, those with functional and organic pathologies of the vocal folds. All patients underwent acoustic voice analysis using the MDVP program, as well as microlaryngoscopy and videolaryngostroboscopy. Multiple logistic regression, XGBoost, Random Forest, Extra Trees, LightGBM, and neural network algorithms (including the TabFPN architecture) were used to build diagnostic models. The quality of the models was evaluated on a test sample (20% of the total sample) using accuracy, sensitivity, specificity, F1-measure, and ROC-AUC metrics. Statistical data processing was performed using Python. The highest diagnostic accuracy (ROC-AUC >0.935) was demonstrated by models based on boosting algorithms and deep neural networks, especially when using the full set of acoustic parameters ( Artificial intelligence methods, particularly boosting and neural networks, demonstrate high efficiency in diagnosing dysphonia based on acoustic characteristics of the voice. Their implementation in clinical practice can increase the objectivity of voice disorder diagnostics and accelerate the process of clinical decision-making. Оценить эффективность различных моделей искусственного интеллекта в диагностике дисфонии на основе акустического анализа голоса, а также сравнить точность и прогностическую ценность алгоритмов при различении нормального состояния, функциональных и органических голосовых нарушений. В исследование включены 1260 пациентов, распределенных в три группы: с нормальной голосовой функцией, с функциональными и органическими патологиями голосовых складок. Всем пациентам выполнен акустический анализ голоса с помощью программы MDVP, а также проведены микроларингоскопия и видеоларингостробоскопия. Для построения диагностических моделей использовались алгоритмы множественной логистической регрессии, XGBoost, Random Forest, Extra Trees, LightGBM и нейронные сети (включая архитектуру TabFPN). Качество моделей оценивалось на тестовой выборке (20% от общей выборки) с применением метрик точности, чувствительности, специфичности, F1-меры и ROC-AUC. Статистическая обработка данных выполнена с использованием Python. Их внедрение в клиническую практику способно повысить объективность диагностики голосовых нарушений и ускорить процесс принятия клинических решений.
